subject.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)

question: Should repeated same-command nonzero exec outcomes ignore all output changes for no-progress detection, accepting that some meaningful changing nonzero output may be blocked at the configured threshold?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent and well-proven, but source inspection cannot decide the product-level balance between stopping runaway failure loops and preserving uncommon nonzero workflows whose output represents real progress.

options.title: Accept stable nonzero fingerprint
options.body: Approve the proposed semantics, rebase onto current main, and rerun the focused foreground and live-agent proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve selected output progress
options.body: Require a narrower maintainer-defined normalization contract for meaningful nonzero output before landing, accepting that volatile failure loops may remain harder to detect.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Keep current output-sensitive behavior and leave the linked bug open until a different progress signal is designed.

recommendation.title: Accept stable nonzero fingerprint
recommendation.body: Approve the proposed semantics, rebase onto current main, and rerun the focused foreground and live-agent proof before merge.
